This
revision petition
is preferred to question the correctness of the judgment dated 16th January, 2019 passed by learned IVth Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (E.C. Act), Aligarh in Criminal Appeal No. 282 of 2014 affirming the judgment dated 20th September, 2014 passed by learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 1, Aligarh holding the revision petitioner guilty for commission of an offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
opennyai_summary.facts:
450 gms of butter was purchased by the Food Inspector and that was divided in three equal parts.
A report dated 6th August,
1991 was received by the Food Inspector from the public chemical analyst and as per that the butter was adulterated.
The report then was forwarded to the Chief Medical Officer, Aligarh who granted sanction for prosecution vide the document Exhibit Ka-5.
On having necessary sanction complaint was filed vide Exhibit Ka-6 before the court competent and necessary information.
The Trial Court by relying upon the statement given by Sri Mohd. Yaseen Khan and the report of public analyst Exhibit Ka-5 held the revision petitioner guilty and recorded his conviction and also awarded sentence to undergo six months imprisonment with a fine of Rs. 1000/-.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The submission of the revision petitioner is that to hold guilty for commission of an offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) it is necessary to establish sale of prohibited article but, in the case in hand, there is no evidence to establish that the revision petitioner was having butter with him for the purpose of sale.
On going through the record, it is apparent that throughout case of the revision petitioner was that he was carrying butter for his own use and not for sale.
It is also apparent from perusal of the record that the revision petitioner was not on any shop or at vending zone or at any permanent station for sale.
He was on his way and was stopped by the Food Inspector.
In such circumstance, the Courts below should have examined the fact as to whether the butter was carried by the accused revision petitioner for sale or for personal consumption.
There is no evidence on record to establish that the butter was carried by the revision petitioner for the purpose of sale except the statement given by Sri Mohd. Yaseen Khan (PW-1), who in cross examination stated that the entire incident is not in his memory being a stale one.
The documents on which the prosecution relied too does not disclose that the butter available with the revision petitioner was for sale.
In absence of the evidence in this regard is sufficient to arrive at a conclusion that no case is made out to hold the revision petitioner guilty for an offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

Aligarh fails.
Hence, the revision petitioner stands acquitted.
The revision petitioner on furnishing sureties and bonds has already been released, which are hereby discharged.
